source.title_on_document: A structured Kano-AHP framework for AI-assisted generative media production: experimental evidence from short-form animation design

supplement.holds: Deidentified expert and audience rating data, AHP weight tables and matrix summaries, group-assignment tables, audience assignment summaries, and prompt metadata (p. 10, Data availability statement). All summary statistics used here are in the main text (Tables 2 to 4).

paper_design_summary: Twenty practitioners (animation, visual communication, motion design) each made one 10-second anime-style vertical clip with GPT-4o and Sora, 10 under a baseline workflow and 10 under a structured Kano-AHP package workflow. Five experts rated all 20 clips and 60 audience viewers each rated eight clips on 7-point scales for narrative coherence, visual style consistency, emotional expressiveness, motion smoothness, and technical quality. Both arms used the same generative AI, so the contrast is between two human workflows around the same tools, and the paper does not say that practitioners were randomly assigned.

studies.label: Short-form animation production experiment (baseline vs structured Kano-AHP package workflow)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Production workflow: baseline (unstructured prompting, revision, and selection) vs structured Kano-AHP package (Kano classification and AHP weighting before prompting and selection); both with GPT-4o and Sora. The paper describes randomization only for the rating procedures: the audience viewers' clip allocation and presentation, and clip order in both the expert and audience evaluation streams. Practitioner assignment is not described as random.
assignment.quote: Twenty practitioners took part in the production phase, with 10 assigned to the baseline condition and 10 to the package condition.
assignment.locator: p. 5, Section 3.5.1 Practitioners; randomization is mentioned only for the audience partial-viewing design and clip order (p. 6, Sections 3.5.3 and 3.7)

arms.name: Baseline
arms.description: Common GPT-4o and Sora toolchain; practitioners relied on their own unstructured judgment to formulate prompts, revise outputs, and select a final clip.

arms.name: Package
arms.description: Same toolchain plus a structured worksheet: Kano requirement classification, consolidation into five criteria, and AHP weighting used for prompt emphasis, revision priorities, and final selection.

participants.who: Practitioners in animation (n = 7), visual communication (n = 7), and motion design (n = 6); mean age 32.05 (SD 4.26); 10 male, 10 female; mean professional experience 5.65 years (baseline) and 5.08 years (package). The 20 counts are assignment counts; the paper does not say the assignment was random. Each practitioner produced one clip and all 20 clips (10 per condition) were rated. Raters (5 experts, 60 audience viewers) evaluated the finished clips and are not counted among the production participants.
participants.quote: Twenty practitioners each produced one final anime-style vertical clip, yielding 20 clips overall (10 per condition).
participants.locator: p. 5, Section 3.4 Experimental design and Section 3.5.1 Practitioners; p. 6, Section 3.6 Study materials

ai_tool.name_model: GPT-4o (ideation and prompt development) and Sora (video generation)
ai_tool.how_used: Text-to-video generation: practitioners drafted prompts with GPT-4o and generated clips with Sora in both arms; 1 to 3 prompt versions per final clip (p. 4, Section 3.2; p. 5, Section 3.4).

task.description: Produce one final 10-second anime-style vertical clip (1,080 x 1,920 pixels, 24 fps, 9:16) under identical output specifications.
task.duration: One bounded production session; session length not stated

contrasts.reported: Expert, narrative coherence: Baseline mean 3.92 (SD 0.83) vs Package mean 5.04 (SD 1.14); mean difference 1.12; Hedges' g 1.11 (Table 2). LMM coefficient beta 1.12, 95% CI [0.73, 1.51], Holm-adjusted p <0.001 (Table 3).

Expert, emotional expressiveness: Baseline mean 3.68 (SD 0.96) vs Package mean 4.98 (SD 1.00); mean difference 1.30; Hedges' g 1.32 (Table 2). LMM coefficient beta 1.30, 95% CI [0.93, 1.67], Holm-adjusted p <0.001 (Table 3).

Audience, narrative coherence: Baseline mean 4.12 (SD 1.16) vs Package mean 4.96 (SD 1.11); mean difference 0.84; Hedges' g 0.74 (Table 2). LMM coefficient beta 0.84, 95% CI [0.65, 1.03], Holm-adjusted p <0.001 (Table 3).

eligibility.reason: Only 20 practitioners (10 per arm) produced output, well below 50; the 5 experts and 60 audience viewers are raters, not participants. Criterion 1 is unclear: the paper says practitioners were 'assigned' but never says at random (randomization is stated only for the raters: the viewers' clip allocation and presentation, and clip order in both the expert and audience evaluation streams; p. 6, Sections 3.5.3 and 3.7), and both arms used the same GPT-4o and Sora toolchain, so the manipulation is a human workflow rather than an AI configuration. Criterion 3 is met: experts and viewers rated each clip on 7-point scales. Listed in the screening report as a small experiment.

one_line_finding: With 10 practitioners per arm, clips from the structured Kano-AHP package workflow were rated higher than baseline clips on all five dimensions, with Hedges' g from 0.98 to 1.32 for experts and 0.74 to 0.99 for viewers, e.g. expert narrative coherence 5.04 vs 3.92 (g = 1.11) (p. 8, Tables 2 and 3).
